ottrelite: A micaceous mineral occurring in small scales. It is characteristic of certain crystalline schists.
ottawas: A tribe of Indians who, when first known, lived on the Ottawa River. Most of them subsequently migrated to the southwestern shore of Lake Superior.
otozoum: An extinct genus of huge vertebrates, probably dinosaurs, known only from four-toed tracks in Triassic sandstones.
otorrhoea: A flow or running from the ear, esp. a purulent discharge.
otorrhea: A flow or running from the ear, esp. a purulent discharge.
otherwhile: At another time, or other times; sometimes; (old) Weighing otherwhiles ten pounds and more. Holland.
ottoman: Of or pertaining to the Turks; as, the Ottoman power or empire. | 1. A Turk. 2. Etym: [F. ottomane, from ottoman Turkish.] A stuffed seat without a back, originally used in Turkey.
otaheiteapple: (a) The fruit of a Polynesian anacardiaceous tree (Spondias dulcis), also called vi-apple. It is rather larger than an apple, and the rind has a flavor of turpentine, but the flesh is said to taste like pineapples. (b) A West Indian name for a myrtaceous tree (Jambosa Malaccensis) which bears crimson berries.
other: Either; -- used with other or or for its correlative (as either . . . or are now used). (old) Other of chalk, other of glass. Chaucer. | 1. Different from that which, or the one who, has been specified; not the same; not identical; additional; second of two. Each of them made other for to win. Chaucer.
otherguise: Of another kind or sort; in another way. "Otherguess arguments." Berkeley.
otherguess: Of another kind or sort; in another way. "Otherguess arguments." Berkeley.
otacoustic: Assisting the sense of hearing; as, an otacoustic instrument. | An instrument to facilitate hearing, as an ear trumpet.
otocyst: An auditory cyst or vesicle; one of the simple auditory organs of many invertebrates, containing a fluid and otoliths; also, the embryonic vesicle from which the parts of the internal ear of vertebrates are developed.
otopathy: A diseased condition of the ear.
otheoscope: An instrument for exhibiting the repulsive action produced by light or heat in an exhausted vessel; a modification of the radoimeter. W. Crookes.
otalgic: Of or pertaining to otalgia. -- n. A remedy for otalgia.
otherwhiles: At another time, or other times; sometimes; (old) Weighing otherwhiles ten pounds and more. Holland.
otherwise: 1. In a different manner; in another way, or in other ways; differently; contrarily. Chaucer. Thy father was a worthy prince, And merited, alas! a better fate; But Heaven thought otherwise. Addison. 2. In other respects. It is said, truly, that the best men otherwise are not always the best in regard of society. Hooker. 3. In different circumstances; under other conditions;
otis: A genus of birds including the bustards.
otobafat: A colorless buttery substance obtained from the fruit of Myristica otoba, a species of nutmeg tree.
otology: The branch of science which treats of the ear and its diseases.
othergates: In another manner. (old) He would have tickled you othergates. Shak.
ottavarima: A stanza of eight lines of heroic verse, with three rhymes, the first six lines rhyming alternately and the last two forming a couplet. It was used by Byron in "Don Juan," by Keats in "Isabella," by Shelley in "The Witch of Atlas," etc.
otologist: One skilled in otology; an aurist.
otolith: One of the small bones or particles of calcareous or other hard substance in the internal ear of vertebrates, and in the auditory organs of many invertebrates; an ear stone. Collectively, the otoliths are called ear sand and otoconite.
otiose: Being at leisure or ease; unemployed; indolent; idle. "Otiose assent." Paley. The true keeping of the Sabbath was not that otiose and unAlford.
oto: A combining form denoting relation to, or situation near or in, the ear.
otoconite: (a) A mass of otoliths. (b) An otolith.
otherwhere: In or to some other place, or places; elsewhere. Milton. Tennyson.
otoscope: An instrument for examining the condition of the ear.
otacousticon: An instrument to facilitate hearing, as an ear trumpet.
otic: Of, pertaining to, or in the region of, the ear; auricular; auditory.
ottoengine: An engine using the Otto cycle.
otocranial: Of or pertaining to the otocrane.
otter: 1. (Zoöl.) Any carnivorous animal of the genus Lutra, and related genera. Several species are described. They have large, flattish heads, short ears, and webbed toes. They are aquatic, and feed on fish. Their fur is soft and valuable. The common otter of Europe is Lutra vulgaris; the American otter is L. Canadensis; other species inhabit South America and Asia. 2.
otoscopy: The examination of the ear; the art of using the otoscope.
otoscopeic: Of or pertaining to the otoscope or to otoscopy.
otocrane: The cavity in the skull in which the parts of the internal ear are lodged.
ottocycle: A four-stroke cycle for internal-combustion engines consisting of the following operations: First stroke, suction into cylinder of explosive charge, as of gas and air; second stroke, compression, ignition, and explosion of this charge; third stroke (the working stroke), expansion of the gases; fourth stroke, expulsion of the products of combustion from the cylinder.
otolite: One of the small bones or particles of calcareous or other hard substance in the internal ear of vertebrates, and in the auditory organs of many invertebrates; an ear stone. Collectively, the otoliths are called ear sand and otoconite.
otherness: The quality or state of being other or different; alterity; oppositeness.
